reason: The idea mostly survives the transfer/leakage lens, because it is a desk rule for choosing finals. It changes nothing in the pipeline. The refined version already sets the lab-to-public slope to k ~ 0 for components that trust the in-sample network, and it builds its private prior from public probes. Public is an unseen embryo, the same kind of data as private, so the lab's in-sample optimism and the 44b6 crop redundancy barely enter mu. The best-of-two principle holds under any sigma: E[D+] >= 0, F1 covers the downside, and a diverse F2 beats a near-copy. Three transfer holes remain in the refined rule. (1) The J-vs-multiplier screen covers only F2 components, but coordhead can enter F1 on its public probe alone. exp51 cuts final nodes 122,704 -> 119,174 (-2.9%), mostly from one 44b6 dummy video (-10.7%). The node penalty is linear and symmetric: adj = J*(1 - 0.1*(Tpred-Ttrue)/Ttrue), from tools/official/metrics.md. So the node drop alone is worth ~0.1*0.029*0.91 = +0.0026, about 37% of x138's +0.007. How much the node count drops varies from video to video. That is the same artefact that turned the stricter min-track-length change from +0.013 offline into -0.004 on public. (2) The sigma formula's in-sample term 0.3*k_eff*|lab| goes to zero when k ~ 0, which is exactly the case for components that trust the edge network. The edge filter would then get s ~ 0.0028 instead of the research note's >= 0.3*|lab| ~ 0.0048. That is not cosmetic: it flips the decision table's 'edge filter in BOTH finals' branch. If ef scores +0.004 on public (private mu ~ +0.003): A (ef in both, F2 adds stitch + cap) gives E[D+] = 0.00107. C (F2 = the F1 stack without ef, + div cap) gives 0.00047 at s 0.0028, 0.00106 at s 0.0048 and 0.00147 at s 0.006. If ef wins only marginally (+0.002 public), C beats A at s 0.0048 (0.00161 vs 0.00107). So whether the one in-sample-trusting component goes in both finals depends on a sigma the formula sets to zero. (3) Screen (ii), 'per-embryo non-negative in the lab', and the heterogeneity term |d44 - d6b|/sqrt2 rest on 2 TRAIN embryos. The detector and linker are in-sample on both, and 44b6 is one recording in 11 leak groups. That is a 1-df, compressed estimate: the 95% CI on sigma from 1 df spans ~0.45x to ~32x. It screens out nothing and measures nothing. The research already found the lab-to-public slope to be -0.06 to -0.26. None of these holes produces a fake local gain, because the rule claims none. They make the chosen pair less of a hedge than it looks. They can be repaired, so this is not a refutation.
fix_if_any: (a) Apply the J-vs-multiplier screen to F1 too. Before coordhead enters F1, compute its multiplier share from the exp51 kernel's per-video node counts: share = 0.1*dN/N*J divided by its public delta. If share > 30%, or the node drop comes mostly from 1-2 videos, keep coordhead in ONE final only. It then acts as the diversifier, not the base. (b) Floor sigma for any component that trusts the in-sample detector or edge net at max(formula, 0.3*|lab delta|): ef >= 0.0048. Recompute the ef branch. If ef's public gain over exp39 is < ~+0.005 (i.e. exp49 <= 0.951), put ef in exactly ONE final and keep the other free of ef. A private failure of the in-sample ILP trust then cannot sink both finals. Stitch trusts the ILP after the filter, so it goes only with ef. (c) Drop lab screen (ii) as evidence: keep it only as a sanity check that no component is negative on both train embryos. For sigma, use the public one-change sd 0.0011 plus the inflated in-sample floor, not |d44 - d6b|. (d) Keep the public floor F1 - 0.003 and the 'no max-public of near-copies' clause. Both are sound. (e) State plainly that the rule adds 0 to the public LB target.
realistic_public_gain: 0 on the public LB. This is a rule for choosing the private finals; it adds nothing toward the 0.97 public target. Expected private gain over auto-picking the two best public submissions: ~+0.0003..+0.0015, largest if probe 29 ties or wins only marginally and ef is kept out of one final. It also insures against a -0.003..-0.005 private loss if an in-sample-trusting or node-multiplier-driven component (ef, coordhead) fails on the other embryos.
